card_asymmetry_disclosure.ruling_ref: RULINGS.md — 'RULED 09-02 16:42Z — F-2 classified from raw: class (ii)'
card_asymmetry_disclosure.sentence_template: card asymmetry — plain claude-sonnet-5 runs max_tokens 4,096 with stop sequences that can fire inside plaintext reasoning (vs 36,864 for the other API models); {N} results ≥ 50% no-code-within-budget rows on hard contest tasks; its new-pool hard-task reliability measures the card as much as the model; counted with their judged verdict under convention (A) — a cut answer fails when its incomplete code fails the tests and passes when its parseable prefix passes them, nothing is forced, and the served numbers include them, flagged; n_truncated beside the result is disclosure only, never a denominator reduction.
card_asymmetry_disclosure.companion_line: wave 1's own sonnet models are clean (0 think-prefix rows, 0 tag-only rows, 3 empty rows in 139,000); this caveat is wave 2's, not wave 1's
card_asymmetry_disclosure.status_line: Resolved on 2 September: those samples contain no code, so their rows count as failures of the model as configured, within its declared answer budget; no hold on the figure and the walk does not censor them; whether the declared budget changes is the project owner's decision, while a candidate run under the larger budget is measured and the served numbers stay the declared budget's. Bridged API models carried no stop reason then, so the cut-answer count undercounted (0 against 1,718 empty answers) until the runs registry carried it; the empty-answer count was the reliable count meanwhile. Three budgets were measured on identical tasks the same night (summary and per-task tables beside; caveats: a single draw against n = 128 means, a selected task set, the declared budget still rising with the corrected re-checks), and the 128k thinking budget on the 580 tasks with the most cut answers (5.5% still cut at 128k, all failing, mostly empty), previewing the redo.
card_asymmetry_disclosure._arm_mapping_rule: Each disclosure key applies to the arms in its `arms` list only; a row renders the sentence(s) of the keys that list its arm, with {N} filled from that arm's feed count. card_asymmetry describes plain claude-sonnet-5's card (4,096 + stops) and applies to claude-sonnet-5_batch only; thinking_cap describes claude-sonnet-5-thinking's 36,864 cap and applies to claude-sonnet-5-thinking_batch only. (Corrected 22:04Z: both arms had been listed under card_asymmetry, so the thinking row rendered plain sonnet's sentence with the thinking arm's N.)

google--gemma-4-31B-it_temp_0.8@768-mark.text: the wave 1 grader's stock prefill renders a completed assistant turn cut at the splitter, so Gemma 4's model turn lacks the thinking-off marker its chat template emits at generation time; a share of sequences then reason inside the code block and loop to the budget. Measured on wave 1 with a 2,048-token cap, gemma-4-12B-it scores 0.677 greedy plus with 50 of 164 answers capped under the stock prefill against 0.927 with none capped under the marker prefill, and gemma-4-31B-it 0.902 against 0.945. The published numbers for both models, on wave 1 and in wave 2, carry the stock prefill and are deflated by it; the same defect on both sides keeps wave 1, wave 2 and wave 2 parked identical. The wave 2 and wave 2 parked runs now generate both models under the corrected prefill as new configuration versions, keeping the earlier legs as disclosed partials; wave 1's card decision rests with the owner (Q13), and until the ruling wave 1 carries the stock prefill, so the two sets differ on these models.

card_asymmetry_disclosure._render_rule: FORM (by ruling of 2 Sep: caveats in tables are flag glyphs only, with the full text on the bound notes page; a missing caveat is a miss; errors go through legitimate channels): in any TABLE the disclosure is a small flag glyph on the affected row only (hover may show the short status_line); the full `sentence`, `companion_line`, digits and ruling_ref render ONLY on the bound companion notes page linked from the flag; the sentence is never printed as prose inside a table or a reader's summary. 'Every surface carrying the arm's numbers' means every such surface LINKS to the notes entry, not that it prints it. BINDING: each arm string listed under a disclosure must bind to exactly one row of the rendering page via the arm-id chain (config_id / board id / hf id / arm_id / label); an unmatched arm string is a BUILD ERROR (or a visible 'disclosure unbound' flag on the page), never a silent N=0 or a missing glyph (alignment look 3 Sep). NOTES PAGE CONTENT: for EVERY disclosure key the notes entry carries the full sentence AND the N line ('N per arm (member frame): <N>' with the frame named), so a reader following a glyph finds the count as well as the share (critic's addendum 3 Sep (peer-reported, minute not given): thinking_cap lacked N). POSITION BY EXTENT (3 Sep, pool-pages-lead's decision, adopted as rule): a disclosure that affects MORE than one third of a surface's rows is a frame property — it renders as ONE § in that surface's basis/caption line (hover = status_line, link = its notes entry) with the notes entry carrying the exposure clause and one aggregate 'N per arm (member frame)' line; per-row glyphs are used only when the affected set is one third or less of the page's rows (they return by rule as heals shrink the set). Drawing a frame property as a row property is the symbol overload the owner called out on 2 Sep. FRAME-LEVEL (3 Sep): a key with frame: true and arms [] is a property of the whole frame — one § per surface in the basis/caption line with the status_line as hover, sentence on the notes page; never row-bound, never 'unbound'.

judge_memory_budget.rule: rows without judge_knobs.mem_pin were judged under a route-dependent effective memory budget (the judge's in-block measurements: cluster about 2.0-2.5 GiB, box about 1.4 GiB; pins deployed on 3 September 2026 at 4 GiB, then the emitter stamp 'min_time_limit=15;mem=8GiB' at 8 GiB effective); unpinned rows stay VALID (ruled stamp of their era), no cell leaves the frame; the repair pass re-judges them under the pinned budget and winner rule v2 takes the higher-tier verdict; disclosure text of record: knowledge/disclosures.published.json key judge_memory_budget (the pool owner's twin)

awaiting_cause_phrases.contradicted-zero: awaiting a valid verdict (contradicted zero, re-judge staged)
awaiting_cause_phrases.contradicted-zero-witnessed: awaiting re-judge (zero witnessed as a judge defect)
awaiting_cause_phrases.tight-route-first-draw: awaiting re-judge (whole-leg zero, judge-side: tight-route timeout)
awaiting_cause_phrases.tight-route-timeout: awaiting re-judge (whole-leg zero, judge-side: tight-route timeout)
awaiting_cause_phrases.dead-delivery: awaiting re-judge (whole-leg zero, judge-side: tight-route timeout)
awaiting_cause_phrases.superseded-version: awaiting a current-content draw (task version superseded)
awaiting_cause_phrases.identity-unresolved: awaiting identity resolution (hash-less draw; mirror re-backfill pending)
awaiting_cause_phrases.withheld-by-ruling: withheld by ruling (wrongly prompted Gemma data is not used; re-runs under the corrected prompt enter as new configuration ids)
awaiting_cause_phrases.refused-on-every-attempt: excluded from the fit intake by ruling of 8 Sep: the Opus arm refused this task on every attempt; the served verdicts and the refusal disclosure stay; this Opus case only
awaiting_cause_phrases.voided-judging: voided judging (the results store's voided_judgings.json names the judging by configuration, shard and judging time: its samples file was not a valid draw when judged; not valid for any store reader; the pool owner's voided-judgings exclusion rule of 7 September 2026)
awaiting_cause_phrases.retracted-by-tombstone: retracted by judging's tombstone row (the store's typed supersede: task, configuration, shard, judging time and stamp named); a retracted judging never competes; the cell waits for a judging that stands
awaiting_cause_phrases.replication-draw: a declared second independent draw of tasks the arm already covers (config_arm_map mode replication, arm none): never pooled into the frame, never serves the arm; kept in out/replication_rows.jsonl for the noise analysis
awaiting_cause_phrases.probe-gate: judge-route probe rows (config_arm_map mode probe, arm none): not a board arm, never joins the frame
awaiting_cause_phrases.closed-configuration: closed partial configuration (no new legs; its banked cells are kept on disk as a disclosed partial and never served or pooled; the successor id carries the arm's work)
awaiting_cause_phrases.recomputed-time-limits: awaiting re-judge (judge-side time limits were recomputed for heavy inputs at this judging instant; the re-judge with the pinned timings supersedes)
awaiting_cause_phrases.torn-partial-api-copy: awaiting re-judge (partial API-leg copy replaced by the complete re-pulled leg)
awaiting_cause_phrases.pinned-zero-tiebreak: awaiting a tie-break re-judge (a pinned re-judge read zero against a lower-tier pass; neither counts until a second pinned re-judge decides)
awaiting_cause_phrases.placeholder-pending: awaiting classification (mostly placeholder samples: extraction vs budget vs truncation)
awaiting_cause_phrases.box-venv-import: awaiting re-judge under the uniform judge environment (judged on the box route while its interpreter lacked part of the pinned set numpy, sympy, networkx, pandas, and the text imports one of them; the judge's heal class of 4 September 2026)
awaiting_cause_phrases.derived-tight-partial: awaiting re-judge (judge-side: pre-heal rows superseded per task where a post-heal valid row exists; the judge's derived-tight-partial window, 4 September 2026)
awaiting_cause_phrases.retired-stamp: judged only under a stamp outside the ruled set (an unruled or retired judge stamp; the rows do not compete until the pool owner rules the string)

identity_coverage.scope: valid rows, all sources; arm-none configurations (replication draws, probe gates) excluded by identity via fleet/config_arm_map.tsv; hashless rows resolve by shard identity
identity_coverage.remedy: upstream: box judge stamps task_samples_sha256 / standing backfill increment (the results store)

pooling.identity: per-task samples identity: task_samples_sha256 (sorted multiset of the task's samples as judged; row field or the backfill mirror); equal (task, hash) = same draw -> latest valid ts; distinct hashes pool; rows without a hash resolve by the shard string (counted); superseded task versions retracted (certify task_versions.json)

identical_pairs.role: retired 2 September 2026 (over-collapsed 228 of 630, missed 94); identity is the per-task hash only

interim_identity.version_retraction_rule: shard rule of record (the pool owner's precedence ruling of 8 September 2026): a row on a superseded shard stands iff its content sha equals the task's current sha; superseded, missing and neither-version shas are retracted

certify_old_only.definition: configs with rows on the superseded shard and none on the task's current shard(s); a cell is (task, config)

interim_identity.old_only_basis: cells whose every VALID row at this build sits on a superseded (task, old_shard); counted store-wide and inside the suite manifest

identity_binding.rule: label (config, shard, task) with one hash binds regardless of host; with two hashes the row's generation host selects the entry (bulbasaur = /workspace-vast/ or runs-relay run_dir; box = devbox re-judge; else charmander); no host entry or n_samples != n_attempts = identity-unresolved, HELD

winner_rule_v2.population_note: all counts store-wide (all tasks and sources) unless a key says manifest; cells_changed_vs_v1 is not monotonic in time: a heal row that is both the latest and the highest-tier judging re-aligns v1 and v2 for its draw

cross_tier_split_by_highest_tier.unit: draw = (task, config, source, samples hash) with valid competing rows at two or more judge-budget tiers
cross_tier_split_by_highest_tier.frames: store_wide = all tasks and sources; manifest = suite-v1 manifest tasks

interim_pin.definition: highest tier 3 (4 GiB pin, the interim era of 3 September 2026)

heal.definition: highest tier 4 (8 GiB pin from the flip of 3 September 2026)

typing_fix.marker: judge_config token typing_fix=v1 AND judge_knobs.typing_fix = typing-builtins-v1 (judging's marker; typing_fix_sha on the knobs when present)
typing_fix.rule: disclosure column typing_fix_share on the frame: share of the cell's pooled attempts whose winning judging carries the marker; no count moves by it; unified_cells.csv cleaned_share, unified_arms.csv cleaned_cells_share + cleaned_rule

timing_wall.field: n_plus_fail_time_limit_only (screens' maker from the attempt sidecar; judgings under the v17.91 time-limit tag only; absent = unknown, never zero)
timing_wall.rule: the pool owner's rule of 7 September 2026: count of record as judged with the time-wall kills beside it; Definitions files the class with the cut-at-cap item awaiting a ruling

interim_identity.keys_deduped_saturated_identical_scope: all sources and arms (API + local); the fit reviewer's 59 = local only

dead_delivery_hold.rule: whole-leg zero-pass at one judge instant (>=5 cells) held out of the pool where the sibling draws of the same tasks mostly pass (mean share >= 0.5); released when witnessed in the windows file

pooling.rule: same samples file: latest valid judge ts; independent samples files: passes and n summed (the pool owner's rulings of 2 September 2026)

frame_of_record.frame_key_note: membership key of record = complete-for-admission AND in_frame (the pool owner, 8 September 2026); one pass admitted five pilot tasks before this key was read: a one-pass frame blip

opus_refused_excluded.rule: ruling of 8 Sep: tasks an Opus arm refused on every attempt do not shape that arm's curve or crossings; Opus only; served cells and the refusal disclosure stay

reader_rule_overlays_and_aliases.partial_guard: attempts first within a draw, then grade, tier, ts

pilot.rule: membership pilot (the pool owner's third set): cells carried in the frame, outside the kept set, the fits, the new-task counts and the plotted sets; the golden preview positions them

fleet_cells_outside_frame.rule: fleet results on tasks outside this frame = wave 1 tasks' results that reached the pool store (bound on the wave 1 side by the census route, never here) + results on tasks outside every kept set (no keep certificate, or not on the kept lists); before 21 Sep 2026 one counter, uncertified_cells_excluded, carried both

plain.uncertified_cells_excluded: results on tasks outside every kept set: no keep certificate, or not on the kept lists

acct.configs_note: configs = distinct ARMS with >=1 manifest fleet cell at build time (stem-normalized); grows with the contest drain

cells_of_record.rule: the pool owner's rule of 7 September 2026: valid_cells.json is the artifact of record for a cell's n / base / plus; no second fold of store rows decides a cell; bind to _stamp, not mtime (the results store)
cells_of_record.windows_stamp: runs/judge/witnessed_windows.json @ 2026-09-23T00:40:58Z (1242 windows; witness-only scopes 535 / ts 587; sibling witness_only_windows 535)
cells_of_record.hold_stamp: runs/judge/rejudge/contradicted_zero_keys.json @ resolved_at 2026-09-23T00:36:03Z (file mtime 2026-09-23T00:36:11Z; 4 hold-flag keys -> 4 draws held in 4 cells; by status {"pending-tiebreak": 3, "witnessed-judge-defect": 1})

arm_map.rule: a configuration with no row in screens' config_arm_map.tsv (or member = false on its census cells) enters no frame and no matrix (the pool owner, 8 September 2026)

cells_excluded_by_census_record.rule: a frame row the census does not serve, named by a validity record in the census header (the tracker's held_cells_index; composed-figure unserved_holds_keys); placeholder cells are counted apart as held by record; never named by the clock

cells_of_record.absent_rule: excluded by a census record: only a cell a validity list in the census header names — the read, never the clock (the pool owner, 21 September 2026, on the results store's reason); before 21 Sep 2026 the winner ts against the census cutoff decided, which misnamed collector lag as absence

results_awaiting_census.rule: frame rows whose cell the census has not served and no census record names, whatever their judge_ts: counted here by configuration, never framed; they enter when the census serves them (the pool owner's word of record: valid_cells.json is the artifact of record; no second fold of store rows decides a cell); with_ts_before_cutoff = rows judged before the census's store read that the collector's copy had not yet carried — collector lag, information, not validity

cells_of_record.cutoff_note: informational since 21 Sep 2026: the cutoff classifies nothing; it only dates the collector-lag count in results_awaiting_census

definitions.semantics: task-pool ruling 09-02 ~16:36Z: rows are FAILURES only if the MODEL produced no code within its DECLARED budget; pipeline-dropped code or infra truncation outside the arm config = artifact rows (invalid; re-extract/re-judge/regenerate). Classification per row from raw completions is Runs' (api-runs) census; this file is the interim flag source.

class.definition: judged sample whose solution is empty, the "<think>" no-parse placeholder, or a <20-char stub because the model produced no parseable code within the arm's DECLARED card (plain sonnet: 4,096 max_tokens + code-terminating stop sequences; sonnet-thinking: 36,864 budget) — a FAILURE of the arm as configured per task-pool ruling 09-02 (class ii), not pipeline loss; changes only if the card changes and the runs regenerate (the gate of the 2 Sep word).

card.render_rule: FORM (by ruling of 2 Sep: caveats in tables are flag glyphs only, with the full text on the bound notes page; a missing caveat is a miss; errors go through legitimate channels): in any TABLE the disclosure is a small flag glyph on the affected row only (hover may show the short status_line); the full `sentence`, `companion_line`, digits and ruling_ref render ONLY on the bound companion notes page linked from the flag; the sentence is never printed as prose inside a table or a reader's summary. 'Every surface carrying the arm's numbers' means every such surface LINKS to the notes entry, not that it prints it. BINDING: each arm string listed under a disclosure must bind to exactly one row of the rendering page via the arm-id chain (config_id / board id / hf id / arm_id / label); an unmatched arm string is a BUILD ERROR (or a visible 'disclosure unbound' flag on the page), never a silent N=0 or a missing glyph (alignment look 3 Sep). NOTES PAGE CONTENT: for EVERY disclosure key the notes entry carries the full sentence AND the N line ('N per arm (member frame): <N>' with the frame named), so a reader following a glyph finds the count as well as the share (critic's addendum 3 Sep (peer-reported, minute not given): thinking_cap lacked N). POSITION BY EXTENT (3 Sep, pool-pages-lead's decision, adopted as rule): a disclosure that affects MORE than one third of a surface's rows is a frame property — it renders as ONE § in that surface's basis/caption line (hover = status_line, link = its notes entry) with the notes entry carrying the exposure clause and one aggregate 'N per arm (member frame)' line; per-row glyphs are used only when the affected set is one third or less of the page's rows (they return by rule as heals shrink the set). Drawing a frame property as a row property is the symbol overload the owner called out on 2 Sep. FRAME-LEVEL (3 Sep): a key with frame: true and arms [] is a property of the whole frame — one § per surface in the basis/caption line with the status_line as hover, sentence on the notes page; never row-bound, never 'unbound'.
card.arm_mapping_rule: Each disclosure key applies to the arms in its `arms` list only; a row renders the sentence(s) of the keys that list its arm, with {N} filled from that arm's feed count. card_asymmetry describes plain Sonnet 5's card (4,096 + stops) and applies to Sonnet 5 only; thinking_cap describes Sonnet 5 (thinking)'s 36,864 cap and applies to Sonnet 5 (thinking) only. (Corrected 22:04Z: both arms had been listed under card_asymmetry, so the thinking row rendered plain Sonnet 5's sentence with the thinking arm's N.)

card_asymmetry.sentence: card asymmetry — plain Sonnet 5 runs max_tokens 4,096 with stop sequences that can fire inside plaintext reasoning (vs 36,864 for the other API models); N results ≥ 50% no-code-within-budget rows on hard contest tasks; its new-pool hard-task reliability measures the card as much as the model; counted with their judged verdict under convention (A) — a cut answer fails when its incomplete code fails the tests and passes when its parseable prefix passes them, nothing is forced, and the served numbers include them, flagged; n_truncated beside the result is disclosure only, never a denominator reduction.
card_asymmetry.N_definition: N counts CLASS A only: the number of the model's results whose class-A row share is ≥ 0.5, where class A = empty or literal '<think>' placeholder judged solutions with no code in the raw. FIELDS in the results store's fleet/valid_cells.json (per result): `class_a_fraction` (alias `no_code_fraction`) = (n_empty + n_think_placeholder) / n_rows; `mostly_no_code` = class_a_fraction ≥ 0.5 — N per model = count of results with mostly_no_code; `class_b_rows` (alias `n_stub`) = import-only stubs whose raw holds a real def after the imports — the extraction defect routed to the corrected-extraction side column, EXCLUDED from N and rendered separately; `empty_or_stub_fraction` / `mostly_placeholder` remain as the A+B disclosure and do not feed N. Row classification source: wave 2 and wave 2 parked critic's f2_degenerate_samples_pertask.json two_class_split (17:52 UK), stamped in the feed's _delivery_defect_hold_stamp.
card_asymmetry.companion_line: wave 1's own Sonnet 5 models are clean (0 think-prefix rows, 0 tag-only rows, 3 empty rows in 139,000); this caveat is wave 2's, not wave 1's
card_asymmetry.status_line: Resolved on 2 September: those samples contain no code, so their rows count as failures of the model as configured, within its declared answer budget; no hold on the figure and the walk does not censor them; whether the declared budget changes is the project owner's decision, while a candidate run under the larger budget is measured and the served numbers stay the declared budget's. Bridged API models carried no stop reason then, so the cut-answer count undercounted (0 against 1,718 empty answers) until the runs registry carried it; the empty-answer count was the reliable count meanwhile. Three budgets were measured on identical tasks the same night (summary and per-task tables beside; caveats: a single draw against n = 128 means, a selected task set, the declared budget still rising with the corrected re-checks), and the 128k thinking budget on the 580 tasks with the most cut answers (5.5% still cut at 128k, all failing, mostly empty), previewing the redo.

judge_memory_budget.sentence: Before 3 Sep 09:29 UK the judge's memory limit depended on where and how the judging ran: a solution could use about 2.5 GiB in a six-core cluster job (about 2.0 GiB in the earlier sixteen-core jobs) and about 1.4 GiB on the shared machine before running out of memory counted as a failure. From 3 Sep 09:29 UK the limit is fixed at 8 GiB for every judging, and from 11:00 UK that day every judging of wave 2 runs at that limit, the same value wave 1 was measured at (8.9 to 10.2 GiB). Results judged before the change stay valid under their own limit; every all-fail result among them was judged again under the 8 GiB limit and the newer judging serves. That re-checking is complete: 273 of 21,724 results changed (72 from the limit itself, 199 from grader corrections, 2 from run-to-run variance; 48 of 6,172 among the results plotted here). A flagged model still has results whose serving judging predates the limit; a larger limit can only turn memory failures into passes, so those results read as judged under the smaller limit.

gemma4_prefill_defect.sentence: the wave 1 grader's stock prefill renders a completed assistant turn cut at the splitter, so Gemma 4's model turn lacks the thinking-off marker its chat template emits at generation time; a share of sequences then reason inside the code block and loop to the budget. Measured on wave 1 with a 2,048-token cap, gemma-4-12B-it scores 0.677 greedy plus with 50 of 164 answers capped under the stock prefill against 0.927 with none capped under the marker prefill, and gemma-4-31B-it 0.902 against 0.945. The published numbers for both models, on wave 1 and in wave 2, carry the stock prefill and are deflated by it; the same defect on both sides keeps wave 1, wave 2 and wave 2 parked identical. The wave 2 and wave 2 parked runs now generate both models under the corrected prefill as new configuration versions, keeping the earlier legs as disclosed partials; wave 1's card decision rests with the owner (Q13), and until the ruling wave 1 carries the stock prefill, so the two sets differ on these models.

output_cap_cut_answers.sentence: answer budget — this configuration's answers are finished to a 4,096-token budget; on the longer wave 2 and wave 2 parked tasks a share of its answers reach the budget that wave 1 never saw (under 2% there), and an answer at the budget passes 0-4% of tests, so the budget sets a floor on the model's failure rate on long tasks; N answers reached the budget before the finishing step; counted with their judged verdict under convention (A) — an answer at the budget fails when its incomplete code fails the tests and passes when its parseable prefix passes them, nothing is forced, and the served numbers include them, flagged; the share is disclosure only, never a denominator reduction; the answers still at the budget after finishing are the live figure beside it (per model, collector-stamped).
output_cap_cut_answers.N_definition: N per model = the model's answers at the budget on the wave 2 and wave 2 parked tasks at bank time, before the finishing step (per_arm[config].n_cut = n_cut_at_bank; denominator n_answers = n_answers_at_bank, its judged answers in the census); the second quantity, answers still at the budget after the finishing rows merged, is per_arm[config].n_still_cut_live of n_live (share_still_cut_live_pct; collector_stamp) — two quantities, two names, never one — the member frame is the stock configurations on the wave 1 card

task_time_cap.sentence: task time cap — the judge ran a task's whole plus set under one clock of about 60 seconds, whatever the per-input limits allow, so on the N tasks whose reference solution itself needs 15 seconds or more over its plus inputs (a loaded judge runs up to four times slower than the pinned timing) a correct program could land as a timeout while a faster-than-reference one passed; ruled: wave 2 route's cap is 300 seconds (task_timeout=300, on since 19:03 UK) and those tasks' results are re-checked; until a task's re-check lands its failure counts carry this flag on every model.

refusal_rows.sentence: The Opus models declined to answer some wave 2 tasks outright (14 tasks, all in wave 2) — 1.5% of Opus 5 answers and 0.2% of opus-thinking answers were refused; the tasks a model refused on every attempt are excluded from that model's results in the fits (not counted as failures there), refusals on some attempts count as judged, and the refusals page keeps the record. By ruling, the tasks Opus refused on every attempt are left out of the Opus models' results in the difficulty fits (they do not count as failures there); the served verdicts stay as checked with the refusal flag, and only the fit intake drops those results. Details: https://ant-devbox.tail94f86e.ts.net/opus-refusals/

header.rule: the task pool PROPOSED stdout-canon clause 16:4xZ Sep 8 (switches FOLD_STDOUT_CANON_MASK = (A) defect-window row more lenient at the stdout_compare knob only against its own same-kind r2 repair; FOLD_STDOUT_CANON_GRADE = (B) the repair competes at the repaired row's grade). cells_flagged = served draw is an r2 repair of a defect-window row (canon_repair); served_judging_changed = the served judging differs from the previous snapshot's; already_serving_r2 = the r2 already served by the ordinary walk (flag only). Passes held at the served grain: row floor = the repaired row's raw + own restores + own overrides, applied only when that row was the served judging of the shard in the previous snapshot (canon_floor_served); cell floor = the previous snapshot's served figure when its draw is the repaired judging (canon_repair_passes_held)

repair_serving.rule: where a cell's served row was graded by the faulty comparison and a corrected re-scoring of the same draw and extraction exists, the corrected one serves; the faulty row's passes are kept (a pass under the stricter comparison is a pass under the corrected one), and the corrected row competes at the grade of the row it repairs; rows of a different extraction never swap

deepseek-ai--DeepSeek-V3.2_temp_0.6.text: Most wave 2 configurations generated with the same output budget as their wave 1 card (stock models a 4,096-token budget; thinking models their own budgets). A few generated under the free-lane launch-table budget of 65,536 tokens or another value that differs from their wave 1 card — DeepSeek-V3.2 chat (65,536 vs 8,192), gemma-4-31B-it (65,536 vs 4,096), Kimi-Linear (65,536 vs 4,096), Moonlight (8,000 vs 4,096) — so for those an answer longer than wave 1's budget is cut and fails on wave 1 but completes and may pass in wave 2. Budgets are the cards that generated each configuration's banked legs, so they are not changed mid-campaign; the difference is disclosed per configuration with the share of answers above the wave 1 budget, once measured; configurations with nothing banked take wave 1 identity (gemma-4-12B-it at 4,096; Kimi-Dev-72B re-cut to its wave 1 card). wording_of_record._render_rule: FORM (by ruling of 2 Sep: caveats in tables are flag glyphs only, with the full text on the bound notes page; a missing caveat is a miss; errors go through legitimate channels): in any TABLE the disclosure is a small flag glyph on the affected row only (hover may show the short status_line); the full `sentence`, `companion_line`, digits and ruling_ref render ONLY on the bound companion notes page linked from the flag; the sentence is never printed as prose inside a table or a reader's summary. 'Every surface carrying the arm's numbers' means every such surface LINKS to the notes entry, not that it prints it. BINDING: each arm string listed under a disclosure must bind to exactly one row of the rendering page via the arm-id chain (config_id / board id / hf id / arm_id / label); an unmatched arm string is a BUILD ERROR (or a visible 'disclosure unbound' flag on the page), never a silent N=0 or a missing glyph (alignment look 3 Sep). NOTES PAGE CONTENT: for EVERY disclosure key the notes entry carries the full sentence AND the N line ('N per arm (member frame): <N>' with the frame named), so a reader following a glyph finds the count as well as the share (critic's addendum 3 Sep (peer-reported, minute not given): thinking_cap lacked N). POSITION BY EXTENT (3 Sep, pool-pages-lead's decision, adopted as rule): a disclosure that affects MORE than one third of a surface's rows is a frame property — it renders as ONE § in that surface's basis/caption line (hover = status_line, link = its notes entry) with the notes entry carrying the exposure clause and one aggregate 'N per arm (member frame)' line; per-row glyphs are used only when the affected set is one third or less of the page's rows (they return by rule as heals shrink the set). Drawing a frame property as a row property is the symbol overload the owner called out on 2 Sep. FRAME-LEVEL (3 Sep): a key with frame: true and arms [] is a property of the whole frame — one § per surface in the basis/caption line with the status_line as hover, sentence on the notes page; never row-bound, never 'unbound'.

card_asymmetry_disclosure._render_rule: FORM (by ruling of 2 Sep: caveats in tables are flag glyphs only, with the full text on the bound notes page; a missing caveat is a miss; errors go through legitimate channels): in any TABLE the disclosure is a small flag glyph on the affected row only (hover may show the short status_line); the full `sentence`, `companion_line`, digits and ruling_ref render ONLY on the bound companion notes page linked from the flag; the sentence is never printed as prose inside a table or a reader's summary. 'Every surface carrying the arm's numbers' means every such surface LINKS to the notes entry, not that it prints it. BINDING: each arm string listed under a disclosure must bind to exactly one row of the rendering page via the arm-id chain (config_id / board id / hf id / arm_id / label); an unmatched arm string is a BUILD ERROR (or a visible 'disclosure unbound' flag on the page), never a silent N=0 or a missing glyph (alignment look 3 Sep). NOTES PAGE CONTENT: for EVERY disclosure key the notes entry carries the full sentence AND the N line ('N per arm (member frame): <N>' with the frame named), so a reader following a glyph finds the count as well as the share (critic's addendum 3 Sep (peer-reported, minute not given): thinking_cap lacked N). POSITION BY EXTENT (3 Sep, pool-pages-lead's decision, adopted as rule): a disclosure that affects MORE than one third of a surface's rows is a frame property — it renders as ONE § in that surface's basis/caption line (hover = status_line, link = its notes entry) with the notes entry carrying the exposure clause and one aggregate 'N per arm (member frame)' line; per-row glyphs are used only when the affected set is one third or less of the page's rows (they return by rule as heals shrink the set). Drawing a frame property as a row property is the symbol overload the owner called out on 2 Sep. FRAME-LEVEL (3 Sep): a key with frame: true and arms [] is a property of the whole frame — one § per surface in the basis/caption line with the status_line as hover, sentence on the notes page; never row-bound, never 'unbound'.
card_asymmetry_disclosure._rule: FORM: render per `render` / `_render_rule` (verbatim from the record): TABLE = flag glyph only, never prose; sentence/companion_line/digits = companion notes page. Text here is the record copy with {N} filled per arm; it is not table content.

awaiting_cause_phrases.placeholder-pending: awaiting classification (mostly placeholder samples: extraction vs budget vs truncation)

class.definition: judged sample whose solution is empty, the "<think>" no-parse placeholder, or a <20-char stub because the model produced no parseable code within the arm's DECLARED card (plain sonnet: 4,096 max_tokens + code-terminating stop sequences; sonnet-thinking: 36,864 budget) — a FAILURE of the arm as configured per task-pool ruling 09-02 (class ii), not pipeline loss; changes only if the card changes and the runs regenerate (the gate of the 2 Sep word).

card.render_rule: FORM (by ruling of 2 Sep: caveats in tables are flag glyphs only, with the full text on the bound notes page; a missing caveat is a miss; errors go through legitimate channels): in any TABLE the disclosure is a small flag glyph on the affected row only (hover may show the short status_line); the full `sentence`, `companion_line`, digits and ruling_ref render ONLY on the bound companion notes page linked from the flag; the sentence is never printed as prose inside a table or a reader's summary. 'Every surface carrying the arm's numbers' means every such surface LINKS to the notes entry, not that it prints it. BINDING: each arm string listed under a disclosure must bind to exactly one row of the rendering page via the arm-id chain (config_id / board id / hf id / arm_id / label); an unmatched arm string is a BUILD ERROR (or a visible 'disclosure unbound' flag on the page), never a silent N=0 or a missing glyph (alignment look 3 Sep). NOTES PAGE CONTENT: for EVERY disclosure key the notes entry carries the full sentence AND the N line ('N per arm (member frame): <N>' with the frame named), so a reader following a glyph finds the count as well as the share (critic's addendum 3 Sep (peer-reported, minute not given): thinking_cap lacked N). POSITION BY EXTENT (3 Sep, pool-pages-lead's decision, adopted as rule): a disclosure that affects MORE than one third of a surface's rows is a frame property — it renders as ONE § in that surface's basis/caption line (hover = status_line, link = its notes entry) with the notes entry carrying the exposure clause and one aggregate 'N per arm (member frame)' line; per-row glyphs are used only when the affected set is one third or less of the page's rows (they return by rule as heals shrink the set). Drawing a frame property as a row property is the symbol overload the owner called out on 2 Sep. FRAME-LEVEL (3 Sep): a key with frame: true and arms [] is a property of the whole frame — one § per surface in the basis/caption line with the status_line as hover, sentence on the notes page; never row-bound, never 'unbound'.
card.arm_mapping_rule: Each disclosure key applies to the arms in its `arms` list only; a row renders the sentence(s) of the keys that list its arm, with {N} filled from that arm's feed count. card_asymmetry describes plain Sonnet 5's card (4,096 + stops) and applies to Sonnet 5 only; thinking_cap describes Sonnet 5 (thinking)'s 36,864 cap and applies to Sonnet 5 (thinking) only. (Corrected 22:04Z: both arms had been listed under card_asymmetry, so the thinking row rendered plain Sonnet 5's sentence with the thinking arm's N.)

card_asymmetry.sentence: card asymmetry — plain Sonnet 5 runs max_tokens 4,096 with stop sequences that can fire inside plaintext reasoning (vs 36,864 for the other API models); N results ≥ 50% no-code-within-budget rows on hard contest tasks; its new-pool hard-task reliability measures the card as much as the model; counted with their judged verdict under convention (A) — a cut answer fails when its incomplete code fails the tests and passes when its parseable prefix passes them, nothing is forced, and the served numbers include them, flagged; n_truncated beside the result is disclosure only, never a denominator reduction.
card_asymmetry.N_definition: N counts CLASS A only: the number of the model's results whose class-A row share is ≥ 0.5, where class A = empty or literal '<think>' placeholder judged solutions with no code in the raw. FIELDS in the results store's fleet/valid_cells.json (per result): `class_a_fraction` (alias `no_code_fraction`) = (n_empty + n_think_placeholder) / n_rows; `mostly_no_code` = class_a_fraction ≥ 0.5 — N per model = count of results with mostly_no_code; `class_b_rows` (alias `n_stub`) = import-only stubs whose raw holds a real def after the imports — the extraction defect routed to the corrected-extraction side column, EXCLUDED from N and rendered separately; `empty_or_stub_fraction` / `mostly_placeholder` remain as the A+B disclosure and do not feed N. Row classification source: wave 2 and wave 2 parked critic's f2_degenerate_samples_pertask.json two_class_split (17:52 UK), stamped in the feed's _delivery_defect_hold_stamp.
card_asymmetry.companion_line: wave 1's own Sonnet 5 models are clean (0 think-prefix rows, 0 tag-only rows, 3 empty rows in 139,000); this caveat is wave 2's, not wave 1's
card_asymmetry.status_line: Resolved on 2 September: those samples contain no code, so their rows count as failures of the model as configured, within its declared answer budget; no hold on the figure and the walk does not censor them; whether the declared budget changes is the project owner's decision, while a candidate run under the larger budget is measured and the served numbers stay the declared budget's. Bridged API models carried no stop reason then, so the cut-answer count undercounted (0 against 1,718 empty answers) until the runs registry carried it; the empty-answer count was the reliable count meanwhile. Three budgets were measured on identical tasks the same night (summary and per-task tables beside; caveats: a single draw against n = 128 means, a selected task set, the declared budget still rising with the corrected re-checks), and the 128k thinking budget on the 580 tasks with the most cut answers (5.5% still cut at 128k, all failing, mostly empty), previewing the redo.

judge_memory_budget.sentence: Before 3 Sep 09:29 UK the judge's memory limit depended on where and how the judging ran: a solution could use about 2.5 GiB in a six-core cluster job (about 2.0 GiB in the earlier sixteen-core jobs) and about 1.4 GiB on the shared machine before running out of memory counted as a failure. From 3 Sep 09:29 UK the limit is fixed at 8 GiB for every judging, and from 11:00 UK that day every judging of wave 2 runs at that limit, the same value wave 1 was measured at (8.9 to 10.2 GiB). Results judged before the change stay valid under their own limit; every all-fail result among them was judged again under the 8 GiB limit and the newer judging serves. That re-checking is complete: 273 of 21,724 results changed (72 from the limit itself, 199 from grader corrections, 2 from run-to-run variance; 48 of 6,172 among the results plotted here). A flagged model still has results whose serving judging predates the limit; a larger limit can only turn memory failures into passes, so those results read as judged under the smaller limit.

output_budget_pool_vs_board.sentence: Most wave 2 configurations generated with the same output budget as their wave 1 card (stock models a 4,096-token budget; thinking models their own budgets). A few generated under the free-lane launch-table budget of 65,536 tokens or another value that differs from their wave 1 card — DeepSeek-V3.2 chat (65,536 vs 8,192), gemma-4-31B-it (65,536 vs 4,096), Kimi-Linear (65,536 vs 4,096), Moonlight (8,000 vs 4,096) — so for those an answer longer than wave 1's budget is cut and fails on wave 1 but completes and may pass in wave 2. Budgets are the cards that generated each configuration's banked legs, so they are not changed mid-campaign; the difference is disclosed per configuration with the share of answers above the wave 1 budget, once measured; configurations with nothing banked take wave 1 identity (gemma-4-12B-it at 4,096; Kimi-Dev-72B re-cut to its wave 1 card). From 17 Sep, models that start on the code tasks are drawn at 4,096 tokens in one pass, while the rows on wave 1 and wave 2 also carry a 4,096-token budget; figures from different budgets are never pooled without both budgets stated.

The published number is base∧plus, which equals the plus verdict there, so it is unaffected; base-only figures are not shown for these tasks. task_time_cap.sentence: task time cap — the judge ran a task's whole plus set under one clock of about 60 seconds, whatever the per-input limits allow, so on the N tasks whose reference solution itself needs 15 seconds or more over its plus inputs (a loaded judge runs up to four times slower than the pinned timing) a correct program could land as a timeout while a faster-than-reference one passed; ruled: wave 2 route's cap is 300 seconds (task_timeout=300, on since 19:03 UK) and those tasks' results are re-checked; until a task's re-check lands its failure counts carry this flag on every model.
task_time_cap.N_definition: N = timed-out attempts under uncapped stamps from the judge's census (attempt-level exposure); the task census digits name the staging priority set
task_time_cap.class: judge identity — the wave 1 grader's whole-task cap (min(60 s, Σ per-input limits)+1) times out correct programs on slow-canonical tasks; TASK-SCOPED, frame-level
task_time_cap.found_by: judging (wave-2 judge-side findings; the task audit's gemini 105/128 on openr1/1366_F was the first symptom), census on the pinned gt caches (charm, 1,977 tasks)
task_time_cap.companion_line: the set is the judge's census of canonical plus-time sums: 19 tasks at 40 seconds or more (10 of them at 60 or more) plus the 15–40 second band added after openr1/1750_F ran at 59 of the 61-second time-out on a loaded judge against 14.5 seconds pinned (a fourfold load factor); residual: a correct solution slower than 300 seconds over the plus set still times out (headroom = 300 / reference sum; openr1/1763_E at 204 seconds has 1.47×, every other task at least 2×), flagged 'cap-bound risk' pending the imported tasks' content decision; the N line reads the mirrored census files
task_time_cap.status_line: judge whole-task cap ≈61 s timed out correct programs on slow-canonical tasks (set: canonical plus sum ≥ 15 s — 19 tasks ≥ 40 s + the 15–40 s band; widened 21:53 UK after a 4× load factor was measured); cap 300 s on since 19:03 UK; legs re-checked task-scoped; flips to landed per task when its results are re-checked · scope: attempt-level since 06:52 UK (credit universal; heal = timed-out attempts under old stamps, census pending)

digits.set_rule: tasks whose canonical plus-time SUM on the pinned ground-truth cache is ≥ 40 s (evalplus's whole plus-set process cap was min(60, Σ limits)+1 s; ruled cap 300 s from the switch); grade +1 set-bound (the task pool task_time_cap); headroom = 300 / canonical sum; cap_bound_risk when headroom < 2 until the imported-tasks record's content decision

canonical_floor.predicate: C′: 4 × canonical total > 100 s (the aggregate cap can bind before the 4× per-input allowance once judge-node load inflates cached timings 3×); C (> 300 s) = 0 tasks; A (canonical total > 300 s) = 0
canonical_floor.held: landing count held at its newest row (2026-09-22T12:25:54Z): the landing file's cluster-side writer has stopped appending (it exited on its seven-day rule; a relaunch through the gate catches up by itself) — the re-judged count under-reads by the landings since then
canonical_floor.basis: class from the judge's task_cap_census.json Cprime_tasks (the set, winner_rule task_time_cap.canonical_floor_2026-09-05.set_of_record); cells = served cells of those tasks in valid_cells with n > 0; rejudged = distinct (config, shard, task) cells in the judge's landing file cap_wave_landings.jsonl whose judge_config carries task_timeout=sum-limits; interim_flagged = cells − rejudged
canonical_floor.flag_text: aggregate cap below the reference's own runtime on this task; fails may be load artefacts; re-check pending

refusal_rows.sentence: The Opus models declined to answer some wave 2 tasks outright (14 tasks, all in wave 2) — 1.5% of Opus 5 answers and 0.2% of opus-thinking answers were refused; the tasks a model refused on every attempt are excluded from that model's results in the fits (not counted as failures there), refusals on some attempts count as judged, and the refusals page keeps the record. By ruling, the tasks Opus refused on every attempt are left out of the Opus models' results in the difficulty fits (they do not count as failures there); the served verdicts stay as checked with the refusal flag, and only the fit intake drops those results. Details: https://ant-devbox.tail94f86e.ts.net/opus-refusals/

judge_noise_floor.measurement: same-samples cross-host judge disagreement, measured 2026-09-02 14:4xZ keyed by (config, task, SHARD) — i.e. one samples file — over every judging (bulbasaur native + charm relay copy): 0 of 1808 keys disagree. The judge is deterministic across hosts on identical samples. Earlier counts (8, then 6) were artifacts of keying by (config, task), which pooled DIFFERENT shards' generations (e.g. certshard_0027_d vs 0065_d, byte-different solution sets) into one key — dual-generation sampling variance, a sampling property, not a judge property (task-audit's byte check, triangulator's re-probe).
judge_noise_floor.ruling: task-pool 2026-09-02 ~14:00Z: identical-input re-judges resolve by latest judge ts (arbitrary, unbiased in expectation); max-pass rejected (selects favourable noise), flag-and-hold rejected (parks noise); identical-input re-judges are NOT corrections and must not be logged as such; a 1-2 sample difference between two judgings is below the measured floor and is never signal
judge_noise_floor.reading: the judge is deterministic on identical samples (349 of 7,196 double-judged keys disagree); differences between two shards' draws of the same task are sampling variance, not judging; the tally's marginal bracket (delta <= ceil(0.03 n)) is a conservative CHOICE, not a measurement

judge_noise_floor_crosstime.definition: CROSS-TIME judge disagreement: same samples file (config, shard, task) judged at ≥2 distinct judge ts with BOTH judgings non-zero; delta = max−min plus_pass across those judgings. Distinct from the cross-route floor (judge_noise_floor.json: relay vs native within the 09-02 heal window).
judge_noise_floor_crosstime.caveat: host is inferred from run_dir (charmander/bulbasaur/charm-relay); node-level host and load are not in store rows — samples_sha256 + host fields are being added to the emitter (runs-lead decision d). Prime suspect per runs-lead: load-sensitive wall-clock timing near the min-time floor.

wording_of_record.status_line: Resolved on 2 September: those samples contain no code, so their rows count as failures of the model as configured, within its declared answer budget; no hold on the figure and the walk does not censor them; whether the declared budget changes is the project owner's decision, while a candidate run under the larger budget is measured and the served numbers stay the declared budget's. Bridged API models carried no stop reason then, so the cut-answer count undercounted (0 against 1,718 empty answers) until the runs registry carried it; the empty-answer count was the reliable count meanwhile. Three budgets were measured on identical tasks the same night (summary and per-task tables beside; caveats: a single draw against n = 128 means, a selected task set, the declared budget still rising with the corrected re-checks), and the 128k thinking budget on the 580 tasks with the most cut answers (5.5% still cut at 128k, all failing, mostly empty), previewing the redo.

wording_of_record._render_rule: FORM (by ruling of 2 Sep: caveats in tables are flag glyphs only, with the full text on the bound notes page; a missing caveat is a miss; errors go through legitimate channels): in any TABLE the disclosure is a small flag glyph on the affected row only (hover may show the short status_line); the full `sentence`, `companion_line`, digits and ruling_ref render ONLY on the bound companion notes page linked from the flag; the sentence is never printed as prose inside a table or a reader's summary. 'Every surface carrying the arm's numbers' means every such surface LINKS to the notes entry, not that it prints it. BINDING: each arm string listed under a disclosure must bind to exactly one row of the rendering page via the arm-id chain (config_id / board id / hf id / arm_id / label); an unmatched arm string is a BUILD ERROR (or a visible 'disclosure unbound' flag on the page), never a silent N=0 or a missing glyph (alignment look 3 Sep). NOTES PAGE CONTENT: for EVERY disclosure key the notes entry carries the full sentence AND the N line ('N per arm (member frame): <N>' with the frame named), so a reader following a glyph finds the count as well as the share (critic's addendum 3 Sep (peer-reported, minute not given): thinking_cap lacked N). POSITION BY EXTENT (3 Sep, pool-pages-lead's decision, adopted as rule): a disclosure that affects MORE than one third of a surface's rows is a frame property — it renders as ONE § in that surface's basis/caption line (hover = status_line, link = its notes entry) with the notes entry carrying the exposure clause and one aggregate 'N per arm (member frame)' line; per-row glyphs are used only when the affected set is one third or less of the page's rows (they return by rule as heals shrink the set). Drawing a frame property as a row property is the symbol overload the owner called out on 2 Sep. FRAME-LEVEL (3 Sep): a key with frame: true and arms [] is a property of the whole frame — one § per surface in the basis/caption line with the status_line as hover, sentence on the notes page; never row-bound, never 'unbound'.
wording_of_record._rule: FORM: render per `render` / `_render_rule` (verbatim from the record): TABLE = flag glyph only, never prose; sentence/companion_line/digits = companion notes page. Text here is the record copy with {N} filled per arm; it is not table content.

render.rule: FORM (by ruling of 2 Sep: caveats in tables are flag glyphs only, with the full text on the bound notes page; a missing caveat is a miss; errors go through legitimate channels): in any TABLE the disclosure is a small flag glyph on the affected row only (hover may show the short status_line); the full `sentence`, `companion_line`, digits and ruling_ref render ONLY on the bound companion notes page linked from the flag; the sentence is never printed as prose inside a table or a reader's summary. 'Every surface carrying the model's numbers' means every such surface LINKS to the notes entry, not that it prints it. BINDING: each model string listed under a disclosure must bind to exactly one row of the rendering page via the model-id chain (config_id / board id / hf id / arm_id / label); an unmatched model string is a BUILD ERROR (or a visible 'disclosure unbound' flag on the page), never a silent N=0 or a missing glyph (alignment look 3 Sep). NOTES PAGE CONTENT: for EVERY disclosure key the notes entry carries the full sentence AND the N line ('N per model (member frame): <N>' with the frame named), so a reader following a glyph finds the count as well as the share (critic's addendum 3 Sep (peer-reported, minute not given): thinking_cap lacked N). POSITION BY EXTENT (3 Sep, pool-pages-lead's decision, adopted as rule): a disclosure that affects MORE than one third of a surface's rows is a frame property — it renders as ONE § in that surface's basis/caption line (hover = status_line, link = its notes entry) with the notes entry carrying the exposure clause and one aggregate 'N per model (member frame)' line; per-row glyphs are used only when the affected set is one third or less of the page's rows (they return by rule as heals shrink the set). Drawing a frame property as a row property is the symbol overload the owner called out on 2 Sep. FRAME-LEVEL (3 Sep): a key with frame: true and models [] is a property of the whole frame — one § per surface in the basis/caption line with the status_line as hover, sentence on the notes page; never row-bound, never 'unbound'.

verdict_rule.rule: (1) VERDICT AS JUDGED on every route and in every reader — a cut answer that still passes is a pass, a cut answer whose incomplete code fails is a failure; (2) still_cut / n_truncated / n_empty_answer are FLAGS carried beside the verdict, never a second verdict (no pass_counted_cut field); (3) the cut share is DISCLOSED per cell as k-of-n (cut attempts of n) until the continuation completes, and per arm by the cap disclosure; (4) NO FORCED FAIL anywhere — by the ruling of 3 Sep (the owner's word is kept in the entry's his_word key); continuation replaces cut samples per sample (merge_semantics) and the continued verdict wins, whichever way it goes.
verdict_rule.store_truth: the fragment writes n_base_pass / n_plus_pass from the evalplus verdicts on the judged text as it stands, records the cut separately (per task n_truncated, n_empty_answer; per continued sample still_cut beside base_pass / plus_pass — raw facts only, no n_pass field), and forces no verdict to fail because a flag is set: a cap-cut answer whose parseable prefix passes the tests is a PASS with still_cut set (api-runs' card36k comparison: 8 of 87 still-cut Sonnet rows are that shape)
